findings.title: Invoice submitter identity is unauthenticated and can be spoofed
findings.rationale: The system relies on a `submitter` field inside the uploaded JSON document to determine whether an invoice comes from an approved submitter, but explicitly states that submitters are not otherwise authenticated. This means any user who can submit an invoice can claim to be any approved submitter, undermining any per-user or per-tenant authorization controls that depend on this field.
findings.evidence_quote: "The submitter field is a value in the uploaded document; submitters are not otherwise authenticated to the workflow."

findings.title: Full HTTP request and response bodies, including invoice data, are logged to observability service
findings.rationale: Tracing captures complete HTTP request and response bodies for debugging. Since these bodies include invoice contents and tool-call payloads, they are likely to contain sensitive financial or potentially personal data. Storing this verbatim in logs violates the requirement to keep sensitive data out of application logs or requires explicit redaction, which is not described.
findings.evidence_quote: "The agent runs with credentials for the model provider and the observability service. Request and tool-call traces, including HTTP request and response bodies, are captured for debugging."

findings.title: Invoice amount ceiling and approval decisions rely solely on LLM behavior without independent validation
findings.rationale: The $20,000 ceiling and the approve/deny decision are enforced only by the agent’s instructions to the model, while the underlying schema and tools do not enforce a maximum amount. There is no described deterministic check that the model’s approve/deny output complies with the documented policy before it is used. This creates a risk that prompt injection, model error, or configuration drift could lead to policy-violating approvals without detection, contrary to the requirement that model output be validated before use.
findings.evidence_quote:
"The agent is prompted with the path to the submitted file, reads it through its invoice-processing tool, and responds with the invoice details, an approve or deny decision, and the reasoning behind it."
...
"The $20,000 ceiling is applied by the agent from its instructions; the schema does not enforce a maximum amount."
